text:
anya: FYI — AcmeProd is seeing intermittent 5xx from the hosted inference API (/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-15T15:00Z. Customer measured ~20% failure rate for a short window. Sample request ids: req_aa1, req_bb2, req_cc3. They included a couple of request traces, pasted below. Can we triage? @mike (oncall) tagging you first. :rotating_light:

mike: on it. Do we know if there was a deploy or config change around 15:00Z? Any quick repro steps from customer?

deploy-bot: deploy/hosted-controlplane v2.14.1 rolled at 2026-03-15T14:42:03Z by ci/cd-pipeline (sha: a1b2c3). No hotfixes after that.

anya: customer pasted this error snippet from the gateway/logs:```
2026-03-15T15:02:11.423Z ERROR gateway request_id=req_aa1 upstream=control-plane status=502 msg="control-plane dependency error" detail="routing-policy-service: timeout after 1000ms"
2026-03-15T15:02:11.425Z ERROR control-plane request_id=req_aa1 service=routing-policy err="configdb read timeout"
2026-03-15T15:02:11.426Z ERROR auth request_id=req_aa1 err="session lookup failed: timeout"
```

anya: they also attached a trace where gateway retried then returned 503:```
gateway -> control-plane (routing) [timeout 1s] -> config-db [p95=2.1s] -> auth [timed out] -> gateway 503
```

lee: I can see a spike in config-db read latency in metrics around 15:01-15:05 UTC from our telemetry (p95 jumped from ~200ms to ~2.1s). Routing policy requests have an internal timeout of 1s which explains the 502/503. Looks correlated with a short burst of read-heavy traffic to the routing-policy service.

lee: Relevant quick metrics (from internal dashboards):
- routing-policy error-rate: baseline 0.1% -> spike 16% at 15:02
- configdb p95 read latency: 0.2s -> 2.1s
- auth session lookup fail rate: increased 4x during window

mike: good find. Any evidence of DB maintenance or slow queries? Could be a bad shard or a transient network hiccup to the config DB cluster.

sara: just checked the ops audit — no manual config changes or schema migrations. No rolling restarts in that timeframe either. We did have a scheduled backup at 14:58 UTC but it shouldn't block reads; I'll verify IO metrics on the config-db nodes.

lee: quick triage steps I'd recommend now:
1) Enable routing-policy fallback so the gateway can route to a default model variant instead of calling routing-policy synchronously. That will avoid 5xx for affected requests.
2) Temporarily bump routing-policy timeout to 2s to reduce immediate errors while we fix config-db latencies.
3) Investigate config-db read queue and IO for hotspots, and add retries/backoff around session lookups.

sara: we can toggle fallback via the control-plane admin API. Sample command:```
# enable static routing fallback to model-small for team AcmeProd
curl -X POST "https://control-plane-admin.internal/api/v1/routing/fallback" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"team":"acmeprod","fallback":"model-small","enabled":true}'
```

mike: I'll apply the fallback and bump the timeout as an immediate mitigation. Applying now.

mike: (running)```
> curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane-admin.internal/api/v1/routing/fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"team":"acmeprod","fallback":"model-small","enabled":true}' 
{"status":"ok","applied_at":"2026-03-15T15:07:12Z"}
```

mike: bumping routing-policy timeout to 2000ms:```
> curl -s -X PATCH "https://control-plane-admin.internal/api/v1/config/routing-policy" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"timeout_ms":2000}' 
{"status":"ok","new_timeout_ms":2000}```

deploy-bot: routing-policy-service replicas: 4 -> 5 scaling event triggered by controller at 2026-03-15T15:08:10Z (autoscale).

lee: After mitigation metrics look better: config-db p95 dropping back to ~250-300ms over next 3 minutes; routing-policy error-rate back under 1%. Auth session lookups success rate recovering.

billing-bot: customer billing unaffected; no billing anomalies detected for AcmeProd during incident window.

anya: Updated Acme Prod with immediate mitigations and asked them to confirm. They replied: "latency looks better, error rate down to ~1% now, thanks." :thumbsup:

mike: marking this as triaged and creating an internal incident ticket for root-cause investigation. Immediate follow-ups:
- (eng-DB) run explain on hot queries and check for recent index changes
- (eng-platform) review backup IO impact and config-db node IO saturation
- (sre) add circuit-breaker + jittered backoff on auth/session lookups in control-plane

sara: I'll take the platform action items — will slot a config-db health check and IO retention check into after-hours window and follow up with a runbook update for backup windows not to coincide with peak traffic for routing-policy.

lee: also adding a tweak to routing-policy: make it async-friendly so gateway can use cached prefix decisions when config-db is slow. Filed PR draft.

anya: thanks all. I'll post a micro-update to the customer with the mitigation details and next steps. Planning a postmortem once RCA complete.

mike: tagging incident channel for visibility: @eng-sre. I'll keep the thread updated if anything else pops up. :eyes:
